    AsrObjectLink

    This class implements an immutable identifier for AUTOSAR objects.

    An AsrObjectLink can be created for each object in the MDF AUTOSAR model tree. The main use case of object links is to identify an object unambiguously at a specific point in time for logging reasons. Additionally and under specific conditions it is also possible to find the related MDF object using its AsrObjectLink instance. But this search-by-link cannot be guaranteed after model changes (details and restrictions below).

    Restrictions of object links

    • They are immutable and will therefore become invalid when the model changes
    • So they don't guarantee that the related MDF object can be retrieved after the model has been changed. Search-by-link may even find another object or throw an exception in this case

    For Classic AUTOSAR

    Object links depend on the MDF object type

    • Referrables
      The object link is actually identical with the AUTOSAR path
    • Ecuc objects with a definition (module, container and parameter)
      The object link additionally stores the DefRef
    • Ecuc parameters
      The object link additionally stores the parameters index. This is the index of all parameters with the same definition below the same parent container instance in the unfiltered model view
    • All other types - feature object link
      The object link also describe paths to all other types in the model by the meta model feature name prefixed with an @featureName. If the feature is a List the feature name is post fixed with the position of the List. The link can also contain variant information. Examples:
      • /ActiveEcuC/Can/CanConfigSet/@adminData
      • /ActiveEcuC/Can/CanConfigSet/@adminData/@docRevision[2]

    Examples for object link strings

    The method getObjectLinkString() returns for example the following strings:
    • For a container, module configuration or all other MIReferrable objects, the AUTOSAR path is returned:
      /ActiveEcuC/Can/CanGeneral
    • For a parameter, the parents AUTOSAR path, the last shortname of its definition and a positional index in the list of parameters with the same definition is used:
      /ActiveEcuC/Can/CanGeneral[2:SomeDefName]
    • In case of variant objects, all variants, this object is visible in, are added:
      /ActiveEcuC/Can/CanConfigSet/CanHardwareObject[0:CanControllerRef]{VariantA, VariantB}
    • For all other elements a feature object link is created:
      /ActiveEcuC/Can/CanConfigSet/@adminData/@docRevision[2]

    For Adaptive AUTOSAR

    Object links depend on the MDF object type

    • Referrables
      The object link is actually identical with the AUTOSAR path
    • All other types - feature object link The object link also describe paths to all other types in the model by the meta model feature name prefixed with an @featureName. If the feature is a List the feature name is post fixed with the position of the List. The link can also contain variant information. Examples:
      • /DataTypes/MyDataType/@adminData
      • /DataTypes/MyDataType/@adminData/@docRevision[2]

    Examples for object link strings

    The method getObjectLinkString() returns for example the following strings:
    • For MIReferrable objects, the AUTOSAR path is returned:
      /DataTypes/MyDataType
    • For all other elements a feature object link is created:
      /DataTypes/MyDataType/@adminData/@docRevision[2]

      • getAutosarObject

        @PublishedMethod
public com.google.common.base.Optional<MIObject> getAutosarObject(IProjectContext projectContext)
        Returns an AUTOSAR object which matches this link. See AsrObjectLink for details about restrictions of retrieving objects by link.

        Remarks concerning variance:

        • When the link contains a variance part ("{variantA}" for example) the object is being retrieved with this visibility. The returned object may therefore be invisible for the caller
        • When the link contains no variance part the object is being retrieved within the callers model view

        Specified by:

        MultipleVariantObjectsException - if more than one object have been found

      • getObjectLinkString

        @PublishedMethod
public java.lang.String getObjectLinkString()
        Creates a string representation of the object link.

        Examples:

        • For a container or module configuration object, the AUTOSAR path is returned - "/MICROSAR/A/B"
        • For a parameter, the parents AUTOSAR path, the last shortname of its definition and a positional index in the list of parameters with the same definition is used - "/MICROSAR/A/B[2:SomeDefName]"

        For objects which are neither parameters nor referrables, the method returns the AUTOSAR path of the first referrable parent object on the root path plus some type information of the object itself.

        If an object is not visible in all variants, the variant name is added to this link (sorted alphabetically).

        Examples:

        • /ActiveEcuC/Can/CanConfigSet/CanHardwareObject[0:CanControllerRef]{VariantA}
        • /ActiveEcuC/Can/CanConfigSet/CanHardwareObject[0:CanControllerRef]{VariantA,VariantB}

        Specified by:
        getObjectLinkString in interface com.vector.cfg.model.base.api.access.IAsrObjectLink
        Returns:

      • getShortObjectLinkString

        @PublishedMethod
public java.lang.String getShortObjectLinkString()
        Implements the same behavior like getObjectLinkString() but omits the parameter index if all of the following conditions apply.
        • The object is a parameter
        • This parameters upper-multiplicity is 1
        • There is actually exactly one parameter present
        The returned object link can still be used to retrieve the parameter by getAutosarObject(IProjectContext) (index 0 is assumed).
        Specified by:
